input.quote: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
input.rationale: Section 7.0 (Materials) defaults all deliverables to Type II Materials, i.e. IBM (or a third party) holds all right, title and interest, and Customer receives only an irrevocable, worldwide, paid-up licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform and distribute copies "within Customer's Enterprise only" (p0085). That fails the preferred position (Customer owns work product created for it, with a licence back for embedded Vendor IP) and also fails the fallback, because the licence back excludes any right to modify/prepare derivative works or to sublicense and is confined to the US portion of our Enterprise per the "Enterprise" definition. The minimal fix is to flip the default to Type I Materials, which already gives Customer full title while granting IBM a broad licence back so IBM retains use of its own know-how and pre-existing Type II IP. Customer Data is not assigned to IBM anywhere ("Content" is defined as Customer-provided and IBM obtains only Required Consents), but there is no express ownership statement, so we add one confirming we retain title to Content and Customer Components and that no Materials are jointly owned.

proposal.summary: Default Materials to Type I (Customer-owned) and confirm Customer ownership of Content
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We flip the default so that Materials created for us during the Service performance period are Type I (owned by us) rather than Type II, and we confirm that we retain ownership of our Content; our playbook requires that we own the deliverables we pay for and all data we put in, with IBM keeping its pre-existing IP. If IBM prefers, we can instead keep the Type II default provided the Type II licence is expanded to a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free right to use, modify and sublicense the Materials for our business.

ops.oldText: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
ops.newText: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type I Materials.

ops.text: e. As between the parties, Customer retains all right, title and interest (including all intellectual property rights) in and to the Content and the Customer Components. Nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers to IBM any ownership of the Content, the Customer Components or any Type I Materials, and no Materials will be jointly owned.
